contradictions.detail: The listing header and features say 'Black Leather Seats / Leather Seats', while the spec section says 'Cloth Upholstery' and the description says 'black cloth upholstery'. Photos and the Sport trim support cloth.

critical_evidence.evidence: No dated records. The dealer's generic 'oil service, brakes and more' does not establish a brake fluid flush by time. A 2021 car is now past the 3-year brake fluid interval.
No transmission records or door-jamb build-date photo. As a 2021 build it has the revised 6MT, so the early-ND1 risk is reduced, but clutch and gearbox history at 61k miles is still unproven.
Floor protector paper is visible in the footwell. No carpet-lifted or drain-area photos. Not examined here.
NHTSA campaign 24V695000 (airbag control module software, 2016-2023 MX-5) applies to this model range. Closure has not been shown.
No tire, battery or service receipts. Sumitomo tires are visible, but DOT dates are not shown.

documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN with a matching decode and an all-in dealer price. A history-report summary is cited but not attached. The maintenance half is absent: no dated records, no brake fluid proof, no recall closure, no tire dates.

condition.rationale: Photos show a straight, clean body and a tidy cabin, with visible steering-wheel leather wear and an aftermarket-looking front lip. Nothing mechanical is stated or proven either way, and the underside, roof drains and tire dates were not examined here.

price_value.rationale: $22,734 all-in sits at or slightly below the $22,804–$24,521 fair-value band for soft-top ND2 cars. That is roughly fair for a 61k-mile two-owner Sport with no records, not a discount.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, reliable ND2 within budget and quick to source. But it is Sport trim and Arctic White, both explicitly ruled out, and a soft top rather than the preferred RF.

logistics.rationale: Dealer lot in La Habra, CA, a drive of about 5-6 hours from Pacific Grove. A mobile PPI should be easy to arrange there. It is a CA car with smog claimed and dealer fees itemised into the price.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Base Sport trim (cloth seats, no LSD, no Bilsteins), a ruled-out white paint and black cloth interior, plus a cosmetic aftermarket lip. The only redeeming spec point is the 181 hp ND2 engine.

Down: evidence of track or autocross use, a slipping clutch, or a branded title.

evidence.mission_note: It is a manual, reliable, budget-band ND2 that could serve as a pragmatic bridge, but it is a Sport in white, both explicitly ruled out. It does not match the RF or Grand Touring target that justifies the accelerated search.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode confirms a 2021 MX-5 Sport soft top with the 181 hp engine and 6-speed manual. The listing cites a history summary of no reported accidents and multiple owners, but the report itself is not provided. Photos show a straight white body, black cloth interior, worn steering-wheel leather, an aftermarket-looking front lip, and Sumitomo tires of unknown date. No dated maintenance, brake fluid, recall closure or tire receipts are provided. The dealer's reconditioning paragraph is generic boilerplate. The $22,734 all-in price sits at the low edge of the $22,804–$24,521 fair band for soft-top ND2 cars. The decisive spec facts are Sport trim and Arctic White paint, both on Jason's ruled-out list, plus a soft top instead of the preferred RF.
evidence.next_action: Before spending on a PPI, confirm with Jason whether a white Sport soft top is acceptable at all. If it is, request the full history report, title photo and recall printout from Dapper Car Sales.
